learningObjective: Distinguish end-to-end model speedup from kernel-level speedup when interpreting the PyTorch 2 paper's `torch.compile` results.

softwareContext.frameworkVersionScope: PyTorch 2.x as reported in the paper

stem: The PyTorch 2 paper reports end-to-end speedups under `torch.compile` on TorchBench-style benchmarks. A reader sees an Inductor-generated Triton kernel that is 3× faster than the eager kernel and infers 'the whole model runs 3× faster'. Which statement most accurately characterizes the reasoning error?

options.text: The reader's error is that Triton kernels never provide speedup over eager on GPUs; the observed 3× must be a measurement artifact and should be discarded.
The reader correctly identifies end-to-end speedup; kernel-level speedup and model-level speedup are always identical when the same benchmark suite is used.

The reader conflates kernel-level and end-to-end speedup. Amdahl's law limits the end-to-end benefit to the fraction of runtime spent in the accelerated kernel; host-side overhead, graph breaks, and non-compiled subgraphs cap the observable end-to-end speedup below the per-kernel factor.
The reader confuses forward and backward pass; end-to-end speedup is defined only for backward-pass time, not the whole model.

explanation: Kernel-level speedup does not equal end-to-end speedup: by Amdahl's law, end-to-end improvement is bounded by the fraction of time the accelerated kernel occupies. In `torch.compile` workloads that fraction is further reduced by host-side Python overhead, graph breaks that force eager fallback, and non-compiled subgraphs. The other options mis-characterize either the relationship (B), the empirical fact (C), or the scope of the metric (D).

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: Triton kernels can and do provide speedups; the error is generalization, not measurement.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: kernel and end-to-end speedups are not equal in general.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: Amdahl-bound argument for kernel vs end-to-end speedup.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: end-to-end speedup covers full-model time, not backward-only.

assumptions: Familiarity with the PyTorch 2 paper's evaluation methodology.
nonImplications: Does not imply Triton kernels are ineffective; they can substantially accelerate certain kernels.
Does not imply that the paper's numbers apply to arbitrary hardware/models.
